ISO_Sculpting.for: The room where authorship changes hands. Every field so far was found — noise, an equation — and here your hand writes one; the two stand side by side so the difference reads as authorship, not technique.
ISO_Sculpting.claim: You never touch the surface in this room: mc_sculpt_vr adds spherical blobs into a float array with a smooth union, up to 500 of them, and the skin is a consequence — while fountain_demo four metres away re-extracts every frame from a time-scrolled field, so what reads as falling water is a run of unrelated solids and nothing in it travels.
ISO_Sculpting.unsure: The two halves are a matched pair on paper (found field vs authored field) but I could not confirm they read that way from inside the room — whether the walk puts the fountain first, and whether the 500-blob cap is ever reached in a session (if it is, the room gains a second argument about the cost of authorship that nothing currently says). blurb.md's opening paragraph ('Seven sculptures rotate in a gallery') has leaked in from room 3 and describes nothing placed here. No intent.md, no critical.md.

ISO_FlatTerrain.for: The hinge. This is where a specimen on a plinth becomes a place you stand under: one added term that reads y, and the ground stops being a graph and becomes a volume with an inside. Portals, caves and the rhizome body all spend the interior this room grants.
ISO_FlatTerrain.claim: The whole turn costs one literal and the shipped value spends it thinly — the book's note on mc_flat_landscape measures 50 of 4,225 columns with an interior at the shipped 0.4, so the heightmap era ends across 1.18% of the floor — while mc_overhang_landscape two steps away runs landform=compound and leans the cliff over your head.
ISO_FlatTerrain.unsure: Whether to re-configure the flat landscape so the interior is visible where a walker actually stands, or whether 1.18% IS the point (the turn is barely there, and saying so is more honest than staging it). This is the sequence's hinge and the room I would least like to be wrong about, and it has no intent.md and no critical.md — the reading above is assembled from tutorial.md, walked.md and the terrain generators. rhizome_cave_system is placed here and resolves to the same scene as room 8's rhizome_cave_demo; it belongs with the caves and does not compete with the argument, so I do not know whether Palle wants it cut or kept as a preview.

ISO_PortalLandscape.for: My reading: this is not 'the portal room', it is the room where a landscape is read term by term as a SUM — base terrain, minus overhang, minus cave, minus arch, plus outcrop — and the ladder hillside / overhung / quarried / arched / compound is the sequence's clearest evidence that a doorway is not drawn, it is an overlap.
ISO_PortalLandscape.claim: The room as built shows nothing room 6 did not: marchingcubes_portal_landscape resolves to marchingcubes_overhang_landscape.tscn — room 6's mc_overhang_landscape — and both are bare tokens, so both run TerrainGeneratorOverhang.gd's default landform = compound; the two rooms are the same landscape, one of them raised six metres.
ISO_PortalLandscape.unsure: THIS READING CONTRADICTS the red-thread argument for this room. I disagree with the red-thread pass about what this room is FOR, and the two available fixes make two different rooms. (a) One config each: `#landform:arched` here and `#landform:overhung` in room 6, and the ladder splits across the two rooms with no scene work at all. (b) The swap: the real portal scene (marchingcubes_portal_landscape.tscn, TerrainGeneratorUnifiedPortals.gd, `density = max(terrainDensity, -portalsDensity)`) is currently placed in room 8 as mc_portal_landscape — the two rooms look like they exchanged their artifacts, and putting them back gives this room its name and thins out an over-crowded room 8. But (b) costs the sequence a claim: those seven torus fields are rung around a fixed circle at TAU/num_portals and written in as their own term, so the portal in them was NOT found by a threshold — the opposite of what this room's blurb says ('the passage was always latent in the field'). No intent.md, no critical.md, no walked.md.

ISO_Caves.for: The critical room. Up to here the surface was a thing to look at; here you stand on the wrong side of it, and the cutoff stops being a parameter and becomes the size of the space you can breathe in. It is where a geometry lesson turns into the project's question: who set the iso-value.
ISO_Caves.claim: queer_marching_cave marches the same kind of field as mc_inside_cave under a shifted threshold (iso_level, cave_density and vertical_bias are all exports on it) and gets another world out — so the room's argument is not 'caves are made of noise' but 'the same data was habitable at one number and solid at another, and nothing in the data forced the choice.'
ISO_Caves.unsure: Five artifacts, the most crowded room in the sequence, and two of them are off-thread. raymarched_metaballs is metaballs.tscn — the same shader placed in rooms 11 and 12 — arguing merging three rooms early. mc_portal_landscape is the real portal scene and is named for room 7. Cutting both leaves the cast walked.md lists plus one foil. What I could not settle is that foil: rhizome_cave_demo is a cave grown by branching rather than found by a threshold, which is a genuinely different logic and pays off in room 13 — keep it as the counter-example, or send it with the other strays? walked.md calls this the critical slot but there is no critical.md and no intent.md, so the political reading above is mine, extrapolated from queer_marching_cave's exports and one walked.md paragraph.

ISO_CaveGeneration.for: The world room: where the human stops shaping places and starts shaping the odds of places. Nobody drew these corridors; somebody wrote a distribution and the field did the drafting.
ISO_CaveGeneration.claim: One of the two bodies in this room is a lie and the room is better for it — marchingcave resolves to marchingcubes.tscn, which sets use_fallback = true (marchingcubes.tscn:47), so the shader never loads and what you walk is a hand-written 200 m sine tunnel, standing beside marchingcubes_cave, which is really marched; blurb.md's 'No artist carved these walls' is false of exactly one of the two, and the honest text is the one that says which.
ISO_CaveGeneration.unsure: Whether Palle wants the fallback fixed or kept as the room's argument — keeping it makes the better room and the worse artifact, and I genuinely do not know which he wants. Second thing, which the red-thread pass does not mention: marchingcubes_cave resolves to the same scene as mc_cave in room 2, so the genuinely-marched cave here is a rerun of the cave that stood beside the fifteen cases seven rooms ago, which weakens the 'graduates to land-maker' reading of the room. No intent.md, no critical.md.

ISO_AnimatedNoise.for: The room that separates motion from re-extraction: nothing here travels, the field changes its mind and the surface is computed again. It is the sequence's answer to the calculus rooms — what looks like movement is the derivative of a field, rendered.
ISO_AnimatedNoise.claim: Neither artifact in this room extracts a moving surface. animated_noise_explorer is placed as a bare token, so it runs its shipped default extraction = 'cells', which fills every straddling cell with a solid cube (917 cells, 5,502 quads by its own header) — the scaffold marching cubes consumes and discards, not the boundary — and mc_base, the static twin the blurb leans on, is marchingcubes.tscn with use_fallback = true, the same drawn sine tunnel as room 9's marchingcave.
ISO_AnimatedNoise.unsure: This is a one-config room if Palle wants it to be: `animated_noise_explorer#extraction:crossings` (or `faces`, which the artifact's own header measures at 26.31% of frame different from `cells`) makes it show a boundary instead of a mass. What I cannot settle is whether the room WANTS the honest version — the artifact's header calls `cells` 'the crude, honest default: a mass where a boundary was promised', which is a strong thing to walk into and might be the better room. Also unverified: the tutorial's 'freeze t with a button' has no control I could find — auto_start is an export, not a switch. No intent.md, no critical.md, no walked.md.

ISO_Metaballs.for: The room where the threshold stops being about one field and becomes about relationship: influence sums, so merging and splitting cost nothing, because there is no topology in the model to break — only a sum and a number.
ISO_Metaballs.claim: Four placements, three scenes, and only one of them extracts: `metaballs` and `raymarched_metaballs` both resolve to implicitsurfacemodeling/metaballs/metaballs.tscn, so the same nine-sphere raymarched shader stands twice in one room, and nakama_metaballs — the book's hero here — displaces a fixed sphere rather than extracting one, pinning its genus at zero, so the hero of a room about merging and splitting is the one body in it that can never split.
ISO_Metaballs.unsure: Whether the fix is to cut one duplicate placement or to make the pair honest by configuring them apart (the shader takes metaball_count, blend_factor, fusion, metaball_seed — two different fusion values would turn a duplicate into a comparison). And critical.md needs a correction pass before anyone quotes it: it attributes 'CPU-driven sphere deformation, sixty blobs' to the `metaballs` artifact when that is nakama_metaballs, and says there is 'no repulsive field' when the tutorial writes one; the tutorial's 'grab one ball' also has no grabbable body. No intent.md and no walked.md; critical.md exists but is partly wrong about which artifact is which.

ISO_ImplicitModeling.for: My reading: this is the CLOSE, not a CSG room. Its job is to gather twelve rooms of the same move — a fog of values, fifteen tiles, described-not-modelled sculpture, authored fields, leaning cliffs, contested thresholds — into one sentence: geometry is never the primary object, only the visible verdict of an invisible field.
ISO_ImplicitModeling.claim: The room cannot argue the boolean algebra it is written around: its single artifact resolves to the same metaballs.tscn as rooms 8 and 11, and metaball.gdshader folds nine spheres with `smin(dist, sphere_dist, blend_factor)` and nothing else — no box, no torus, no min, no max, no subtraction — so of union / intersection / subtraction the closing room performs exactly one, and 'sixteen tiles of implicit logic' places nothing.
ISO_ImplicitModeling.unsure: THIS READING CONTRADICTS the red-thread argument for this room. I disagree with the red-thread pass about this room's core. It reads it as an artifacts room whose artifact is wrong; I read it as a relation room, because the only text that is TRUE today is about the sequence, not about this shader. If Palle wants the CSG room instead, that is a new artifact — a station with a box, a torus and three operators — and it is the single largest piece of work this sequence needs. Second thing I could not settle: walked.md flags an open 'seed slot' here (no room hands the movable-threshold verb forward), but that text was written before ISO_RhizomeBody existed, so I do not know whether room 13 now fills it, and therefore whether room 12 or room 13 is the sequence's close. critical.md exists — 719 words of Simondon on a shader that does not perform the operations it describes.

ISO_RhizomeBody.for: The payoff room, and the sequence's only building. Everything before it was a field you looked at or stood beside; here the field IS the plan, and the walk out is through the body. It answers room 12's claim by taking it literally — describe a building instead of drawing one, then walk in.
ISO_RhizomeBody.claim: The hollow is the same equation as the lump: abs(f) - wall gives an outer skin, an inner skin and nothing between, so the walkable void is the solid's own interior and no corridor was ever drafted — 8 chambers, 10 passages, cycle rank 3, which means no root and no single route — and the wayfinding is the anatomy, since every marched vertex carries which limb is nearest and how close the runner-up came, so colour says which limb you are in and light says where it fused.
ISO_RhizomeBody.unsure: This is the least-read room in the sequence and the brief is a GUESS built from blurb.md plus the registry entry, not from a pass over the room: no tutorial.md, no intent.md, no critical.md, no walked.md, no pearl in commons/data/book/isosurfaces.json, and no artifact_group in commons/maps/sequences/isosurfaces.json. Two things I want ruled. (1) The map is an empty 34x34 hall with a 25 m body in it and one spawn and one teleporter in the whole utility layer; the design note says finding the bored mouth (MOUTH_R 1.75, a 3.5 m ovoid) is the first move the map asks for — is that meant to be hard, and is anything supposed to point at it? (2) Whether this room or ISO_ImplicitModeling is the sequence's close; both are currently written as one, and the two texts will fight unless one of them yields.

WaveFunctions_Intro.for: Opens the sequence by fixing a vocabulary before any physics explains it: one signal, read four ways at once — as height, as spin, as scale, and as a diagram on a screen. No other room asks you to hold four readings of one motion.
WaveFunctions_Intro.claim: The whole grammar is one component swap standing in a row: transformation_cube at (4,3) bobs, rotating_cube at (4,5) spins, and everything else on the floor — y_oscillation_cube, rotating_cube_demo, oscillation_controlled_cube driven by control_pendulum two rows down — is a variation on that difference.
WaveFunctions_Intro.unsure: The blurb and tutorial.md describe a room that is not built: 'a small room lined with oscilloscopes... sine, square, sawtooth, triangle', Hooke springs, a `render_trace` to a Line2D. Nothing like it is placed — the only display in the map is one `science_screen:180:1.5#mode:wave` at (5,7), which the registry says projects a NEARBY 3D artifact into 2D, so it is a mirror of the cubes, not an instrument bank. Two things I could not read: the five `pick_up_cube` at y-offsets 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0 down rows 11-15 form a LINEAR ramp, not an oscillation — deliberate counter-example (steady rise versus return) or leftover? And cols 9-11, rows 1-20 is a 3x20 sealed floor corridor with no entrance (pathfinder: 133 of 286 cells reachable) — dead space or something once planned?

WaveFunctions_Pendulum.for: Grounds the sine in a mechanism nobody designed — gravity and a string are enough — and gives the sequence its first RECORDING instruments, so a motion can be read after it has stopped.
WaveFunctions_Pendulum.claim: The room's real subject is the trace, not the swing: three pendulums write their own motion down (PendulumWave phase-separated by length, foucault_pendulum onto the floor, WavePaintings by double-pendulum brush), and the only artifact standing inside the raised arena you ride a `tc:3:y` lift to reach is draw_dot_time_domain — the recorder, alone on the stage.
WaveFunctions_Pendulum.unsure: Whether the room is about inevitability (blurb, intent) or about recording (my reading, from where things stand) is the call I cannot make for you. The blurb omits WavePaintings entirely, which the book makes the hero and which is the sequence's only chaotic station — determinism you cannot predict, sitting in a room whose argument is that oscillation is predictable. And no text anywhere mentions the map's most distinctive shape: a sunken 2-high arena inside a 4-high rim at rows 5-9, reached by two transport-cube lifts at (8,2) and (8,9). Is that a pit you look into or a stage you stand on?

WaveFunctions_Unit_Circle.for: The sequence's thesis room — the only place that says where sine COMES FROM rather than what it does, and the room every later room cites when it cites anything at all.
WaveFunctions_Unit_Circle.claim: Source, output and floor are placed in one row so they land in one glance — unit_circle_advanced at (1,1), SimpleOscillatingBridge at (1,5), OscillationCurve at (1,11), all on the north strip above a 6x9 pit — but the map has no `s` cell and no `spawn_points` block, and GridSpawnComponent's default is the raw floor centroid with no snapping, which for this map is (row 6.3, col 6.0): a void cell.
WaveFunctions_Unit_Circle.unsure: I have not walked it. The pathfinder reports 1 of 125 cells reachable and every primary artifact plus the teleporter unreachable, which is exactly what a spawn on the island at (4,6) or a fall into the pit would produce — but a pathfinder warning is not a fall, and this is the hinge, so it is worth a headset before an afternoon goes into the prose. Second, unresolved and older: intent.md calls this 'Fourth map... follows WaveFunctions_Sine_Space' while wavefunctions.json runs it third, before Sine_Space. Every intent.md and tutorial.md in the sequence uses one order and the sequence file uses the other. Whichever way it goes, this room's text will name a neighbour, so the ruling has to come first.

WaveFunctions_Sine_Space.for: The room where the sine stops being a graph and becomes a place — the sequence's one claim that you can be INSIDE a function instead of looking at it from outside.
WaveFunctions_Sine_Space.claim: Exactly one artifact makes that true: sine_wall_corridor at (3,7), two layered sine walls a phase apart with the second built by mirroring the first. The other twenty-two rows of the map are a flat 1-cell catwalk down col 10, beside an 8-wide, 18-long trench with sine_space and three colorballs at the bottom — so the map argues the floor is the wave and then gives you a straight one to walk.
WaveFunctions_Sine_Space.unsure: Whether that is the fault or the point. Read generously it is a good sequence — you walk the wave once at the entrance, then walk beside it and look down on what you were inside. Read plainly, the corridor is over in four rows and the rest is a viewing gallery. I cannot tell which you built. Also: no `s` cell, and the floor centroid lands at (row 13.9, col 6.7), inside the trench. And blurb.md says the colorballs 'mark phase positions' — the registry says N rigid physics spheres from a named palette, so they mark nothing; three of them sit in the trench at rows 8, 13 and 18.

WaveFunctions_3D_Wave_Propagation.for: Turns oscillation from something that happens HERE into something that spreads — the room that swaps the object for the medium, and the last room of the sequence's first chain.
WaveFunctions_3D_Wave_Propagation.claim: The room is a 13x13 hole with a one-cell rim, and all three artifacts hang inside it, so you meet the medium from outside it — and the artifact that actually states the lesson, coupled_oscillator_lattice at (13,7) ('a wave is not a particle traveling — it is a pattern of agreement across coupled cells; the lattice IS the medium'), is the one no text in the map names.
WaveFunctions_3D_Wave_Propagation.unsure: Whether standing outside the field is the design (a pattern is only visible from outside it — which would be a good sentence) or an accident of the void. Separately, blurb.md says kusama_sine 'stipples the field with polka-dots displaced by the wave'; kusama.gd is a standalone pulsing sculpture that never reads the field, so that sentence is untrue as placed and should not survive into final.md.

WaveFunctions_Effect_Sound.for: The sequence's turn from waves you see to waves you hear — and, as built, the only room in wavefunctions where something comes at you.
WaveFunctions_Effect_Sound.claim: This is not a room with an argument but a store with five: chiptune waveform-shaping (three MarioSoundController presets — techno_kick, laser_zap, sine_bell), additive timbre (timbre_sculptor#waveform:square), consonance (chord_tension_spring, harmonic_distance_table), spatial interference (wave_interference_3d), and a three-body foe encounter (catalyst_vent#wave_size:3 at (6,8), five seconds after you arrive) — 37 placements, and the only group that shares a claim is the four synth racks standing shoulder to shoulder at row 5.
WaveFunctions_Effect_Sound.unsure: I do not disagree with the room, I disagree with its blurb: it argues quantisation noise and latency, and nothing placed measures either. The question only you can settle is the vent. catalyst_vent plus catalyst_prompter_box#emergence:vent#lease_s:45 put a foe fight in the middle of a sound lab; the chambers left the spine on 2026-09-02. Is this encounter a survivor of that removal that should be cut, or is a wave that attacks you the point of the room? It changes what the text is about — a depot to be triaged, or a room that turns sound into a hazard. Two further unnamed placements postdate every text here: rack_room at (5,6) and interactable_demo at (11,11), the latter a registry-described 'inspection rig laying out one of every VR control type'.

Wavefunctions_Bernini.for: The sequence's one art-historical room, and the only room in wavefunctions that changes the visitor's body — where a waveform stops being read and starts being worn.
Wavefunctions_Bernini.claim: The Elphaba dress is in this room twice: hanging on nobody at (4,7) as an artifact, and on YOU — `pb:dress` at grid (1,0) calls PlayerCustomization.give_dress(), which instantiates the same res://algorithms/wavefunctions/dancing_body/ElphabaDress.tscn onto the player's XROrigin at hip height, one cell from where `m:` drops you on arrival.
Wavefunctions_Bernini.unsure: THIS READING CONTRADICTS the red-thread argument for this room. Three things. (a) `core` could as fairly be `artifacts`: bernini_columns states the room's title lesson on its own — a spiral column is a sine wrapped around a vertical axis — and needs no utility layer. I chose `utilities` because the dressing is the room's one unrepeated event and no artifact token carries it, but this is exactly the field to correct me on. (b) I could not confirm the dress lands. `m:1:4:1:0.1` parses under the current `m:` reader as delay 1.0 with '4:1:0.1' ignored, dropping you at the m: cell (0,0) — a 2-high block in the NW corner, with the pb:dress block next to it. It looks intentional; it wants a walk. (c) vowel_sound_board is set to say 'right here, right now' on repeat and no text explains it. Cut it, or write the vocal tract as a column of air.

WaveFunctions_John_Cage.for: The counterweight — after seven rooms of accumulating oscillation, the room that asks what is left when you stop producing it, and answers that you cannot get to zero.

What the sculpture is listening to is the composer's own recording, not the room.

Answering it decides whether final.md describes the room that exists or the room that was designed — and it is the difference between an afternoon and two. WaveFunctions_AirMusic.unsure: (a) The room is a donut around a 5x5 pit, and the generative engine (SystemsMusicTest at (5,5)) is placed INSIDE the pit, with the one island cell at (4,5) unreachable beside it, while every instrument you can touch — RackAmbientDrone, air_music_display_case, resonating_metallophone — is on the south floor. Is the music meant to hang over the hole? (b) No `s` cell; the floor centroid lands at (5.5, 6.2), in that pit. If you would rather the room's text stay to what a body can see, say so now — the durations are the strongest thing here and they photograph as nothing.

Wavefunctions_Sky_Stairs.for: The sequence's one vertical room — where the wave stops being something you cross a floor to see and becomes something that costs you a climb, measured in the legs rather than on a graph.
Wavefunctions_Sky_Stairs.claim: The map is named for a sine and does not contain one. sine_cylinder_staircase ships `WAVE_AMPLITUDE: float = 0.0  # set >0 for wavy path`, and `_compute_samples()` computes `wave := sin(ang * WAVE_FREQUENCY) * WAVE_AMPLITUDE` — so with the map placing it bare as `sine_cylinder_staircase:0:-2.5`, the radius is a constant 2.5 and what you climb is a plain 80-step, 2-turn, 8 m helix. A circle projected upward, with the sine switched off.
Wavefunctions_Sky_Stairs.unsure: THIS READING CONTRADICTS the red-thread argument for this room. Whether that is a bug or the room's best sentence. Read one way it is a gift: Sky Stairs IS the Unit Circle standing up, the sine was never needed, and the blurb already says 'The stairs are the rotation, projected upward.' Read the other way the room is titled Sine Curve Staircase and wants `#WAVE_AMPLITUDE:0.4` in the placement. I cannot pick for you and the text differs completely either way. Note also there are now three staircases in this room's paperwork: the modulated helix in the code, a straight 15 m flat sine graph in tutorial.md (60 steps at y = amplitude·sin(TAU·f·x), no rotation anywhere), and the plain helix actually built. And the artifact's shipped `provision` is 'membrane' — magenta translucent quads its own axis note calls 'scaffolding left in place' — which is what a climber's foot actually meets.

WaveFunctions_TrigWalkingPath.for: Picks the circle back up after five rooms of applications and hands the sequence to Fourier — the room that puts two oscillations side by side so the RELATION between them, not either one, is the object.
WaveFunctions_TrigWalkingPath.claim: Every artifact here is two oscillations held against each other and nothing else: the two lanes at sin and cos a quarter turn apart, beat_frequency_demo (two near-identical frequencies whose difference becomes the loudest thing), lissajous_curves (a ratio that either closes or wanders forever), wave_interference (two fronts summing), sine_oscillation (a circle and its two projections) — five statements of one sentence, and the sequence's only room with no dilution in it.
WaveFunctions_TrigWalkingPath.unsure: (a) The blurb's second paragraph is about a different room: it names pendulums, 'a double pendulum grid' of nine diverging systems, and DNA from two half-cycle-shifted helices. None of those is in map_data.json. It has to be rewritten to the five placed tokens before final.md quotes it. If you read the room as Unit Circle's reply, the text is written as a reply and the form changes.

WaveFunctions_Synthesis_Lab.for: Cashes the sequence's stated truth — every signal is a sum of sines — and is the only room that lets you BUILD one rather than watch one, then shuts the loop back to the hinge.
WaveFunctions_Synthesis_Lab.claim: Four instruments carry the theorem and all four stand at floor height — additive_wave_demo at (6,2), oscilloscope at (8,10), chladni_plate at (11,7), and UnitCircleTrig at (2,10), which returns the room to the unit circle — while six of the lab's 26 placements stand on top of 4 m walls and two sit in a void, so roughly a third of the room is scenery you cannot reach.

The pathfinder confirms atmosphericmonitoring, chemicalapparatus and multimeter are unreachable. (b) The blurb promises 'a square wave emerge from pure curves'; the placement is `additive_wave_demo:0:0.5#waveform:sawtooth`. Which one is the room? (c) Two placements postdate every text here and are named nowhere: record_room at (3,6), and `synthesis_stand#subject:hallway_scene#mode:hero` at (4,10) — a measurement-verdict stand pointed at hallway_scene rather than at anything this sequence argues. I do not know whether it belongs in the finale. (d) The blurb's 'six vials pulse in phase sequence' is samplevialrack, which is placed in the void at (8,9).

Random_Noise_Types.for: The only room in the sequence where randomness has not yet learned to remember its neighbours. It splits "random" into kinds — uniform, gaussian, blue — so that everything from Noise_Columns onward has a null condition to be measured against.

ML_Sequence_Memory.for: Puts time inside the machine, and does it in a corridor 2 cells wide and 12 rows deep, so the walk itself is the recurrence the transformer standing in it abolishes.
ML_Sequence_Memory.claim: You meet the transformer first (r5 c1) and the LSTM second (r8 c0), which reverses the order the blurb and tutorial teach — so the room as walked argues attention is the default and gating is the older workaround, not the other way round.
ML_Sequence_Memory.unsure: I can't tell whether that order is a ruling or a by-product: the primary order for this map is a floor default (n_ruled = 0) and row-major reading happens to give transformers_vr first. If LSTM-then-transformer is the lesson, the two placements should swap and my claim inverts. ML_Generative.for: The turn from judging to making, staged as a split room: an h3 divider at cols 3-4 with a gap at rows 3-4, so you cross from the generator's side to the discriminator's side on your way to the exit.

ML_Generative.unsure: I don't know whether the empty east half is a gap or the point. Either it wants the VAE the blurb's second paragraph promises (no VAE token is placed and I found none wired for this map), or the emptiness IS the argument — nothing stands on the discriminator's side because the discriminator has no access to the world, which is what critical.md says: "The system that learns to produce reality has no access to reality." The second reading makes better prose and a harder claim, and I'd rather you ruled than I guessed. Second: generative_adversarial_networks_gans_vr declares no DNA axis, so there is no variant to set. ML_Synthesis.for: The last room, and the only one that adds no technique: three islands over void where the tools turn back on themselves — a body learning itself, a model of belonging, a model asked to explain.
ML_Synthesis.claim: The room is held up by its crossings, not its floor — tc:5:x at r2 c3 and tc:5:z at r7 c8 are the only ways between the islands, and the exit at r9 c9 is a teleporter on a void cell, so the sequence ends by dropping you through the thing it was standing on.
ML_Synthesis.unsure: THIS READING CONTRADICTS the red-thread argument for this room. Two things I could not settle. (1) Geometry: joint_learn_walk (r2 c6) and explainable_ai_xai_vr (r7 c2) both sit on structure cells whose value is "0" — void — at y_offset 2. anomaly_detection (r2 c2) is the only one on solid floor, and it is also the nearest to spawn, two cells away. The book pearl note says "the anomaly detector exiled furthest out"; the grid says the opposite, and I think the note is wrong. Whether two artifacts hovering over void is intended — you fly past joint_learn_walk on the tc:5:x ride rather than standing at it — or a placement fault, I can't tell, and it changes the whole room. (2) core: I chose `utilities` because the crossings are what make the room walkable and what critical.md's closing paragraph is actually about, but `relation` is arguable — this room means what the seven before it mean — and that choice changes the form of the text. Also tutorial.md gives five of seven blocks to Q-learning/REINFORCE for one island and nothing to thresholds or attribution for the other two.

GT_Foundations.for: Open the sequence by performing its one move in public: throw the world away, keep only what connects to what, and settle a question by counting before any search starts. It is also the only room that puts the general case (graphspace, graphspace3d) on the floor beside its single famous instance.
GT_Foundations.claim: The room answers its own question before you have walked it — four odd-degree landmasses, so no route exists — while the floor you cross to hear that is a path with no cycles: four landmasses joined by three transport cubes and one 1-wide bridge along col 5, walkable exactly once. The impossible walk is on the plinth; the possible one is under your feet.
GT_Foundations.unsure: I disagree with the red-thread pass's evidence on graphspace3d. It calls it 'the bare token' — true of the registry description, which is the literal string 'graphspace3d' — but the token points at graphspace3d.tscn, and KonigsbergBridge points at konigsberg3d.tscn, whose class Konigsberg3D extends GraphSpace3D. So the room holds the general 3D graph standing next to its own specialisation, which is the room's subject, not an echo. Two things I could not settle: (1) whether the floor's Eulerian-path shape is authored or accidental — NW island (rows 1-3, cols 1-3) -> ferry at (2,3) -> the col-5 spine and centre island -> row-5 bridge and ferry at (5,9) -> east column -> SE island: a tree, so every bridge is crossable once, which is exactly what Konigsberg denies. If it is accidental it is still the best sentence available and I would write it; Palle should say. (2) synthesis_stand#subject:graphspace#mode:hero sits at (1,5), three cells from graphspace itself at (2,2) — a hero stand of a thing you can see from it. Deliberate double, or leftover? It is the only placement in all eight rooms carrying a config token.

GT_Layout.for: Run the opening squint backwards — take pure relation and let it grow a body — and be the room that admits the picture is an algorithm's opinion, not the graph. It is where the sequence borrows the Forces chapter back.
GT_Layout.claim: The room's lesson is a number rather than a metaphor: tutorial.md's layout_stress() measures the mismatch between graph distance and drawn distance, so the room can state exactly how much its own picture lies. The two force-directed artifacts are not a repeat — force_directed_layout at (4,5) and forcedirected3d at (10,8) sit at opposite ends of the same diagonal walk, the same physics in 2D then in 3D.
GT_Layout.unsure: I disagree with the thread on 'the two force-directed artifacts double each other'; six cells and the whole walk separate them and the second adds a dimension, which reads as progression. What I could not settle is the floor. Only 64 of 195 cells are reachable — the map is a narrow diagonal staircase cut through a solid block of h5, not the 'platforms at irregular heights, no symmetry, no grid' the blurb promises. A staircase is the one shape a settled force-directed graph never makes, so either the floor is wrong for the room or the blurb is describing a map that was never built, and I cannot tell which Palle wants fixed. Also open: graph_basilica at (12,6) is a walk-in building that IS a graph with a BFS light-wave rolling through it — that may be the room's best exhibit (a layout you stand inside) rather than the stray the thread calls it. force_directed_layout ships graph: "cube", the most regular of its five test graphs; "clique" or "bipartite" would give the springs something to argue about.

GT_Pathfinding.for: Turn the sequence from a subject into infrastructure. This is the room where graph search stops being an exhibit and is revealed as the thing that decides, for every map in this project, whether a room counts as a place at all — the hinge, and the one room built as honestly as its blurb.
GT_Pathfinding.claim: The room about search ships with the search not run, and the floor is doing the searching instead. pathfinding3d places at its default frontier: "unsearched", which its own source defines as "the maze alone... nothing between them. Exactly what ships today, because _ready() has never called start_pathfinding()" — while grid_substrate_runner at (11,2) mounts mutators on the map's own GridMultiMesh at floor_plan_mode PATH_GUARANTEE, BFS-filling the cheapest cubes needed to keep spawn-to-teleporter walkable as the pattern cycles.
GT_Pathfinding.unsure: The dossier's evidence for this room never mentions grid_substrate_runner, which I think is the strongest thing in the sequence: walked.md's turn ('the exhibit is the examiner') is a shipped mechanic here, not a metaphor, and nobody has written it down. I read PATH_GUARANTEE off the export default; I have not walked the room, so I do not know whether it is legible in play or just quietly true. Second: this is two rooms. Cols 1-7 are a real maze of h5 walls with 1-wide corridors and dead ends holding pathfinding3d; cols 8-11 are a flat 4x11 open field holding the other four artifacts. I cannot tell whether the open half is a deliberate plain where the maze's lesson is restated at four scales, or a dumping ground. Third: none of the three core values names the structure layer, and half this room's teaching is the maze itself. I picked artifacts; if there were a fourth value I would pick it. Fourth: pathfinding3d's frontier axis has expanded (~23 cells) and flooded (~1200 cells) returning the SAME path — the cost of not guessing, as volume. That is a whole room's argument sitting unused in one export.

GT_Network_Analysis.for: Pair measurement with its refusal in one room — the only place in the sequence where an artifact stands against the question the room is asking, and the last room before the thread frays.
GT_Network_Analysis.claim: The room already stages that argument in its layers and nobody has said so: you spawn at (1,1) on a detached 2x2 island with rhizomatic_structure, ride a transport cube (tc:4:x) to the hub, and both measuring instruments — network_analysis at col 2 row 8, networkflow3d at col 5 row 8 — are placed on structure height 0. They are showpieces over void. The critique is the only artifact in the room you can stand on.
GT_Network_Analysis.unsure: Two things I could not settle. (1) Whether the void placement is authored or two separate accidents. The pathfinder passes this map because Rule 4 skips h=0 artifacts as display pieces, and the geometry differs: networkflow3d is one cell west of the south arm and readable from the path, while network_analysis is five cells from any floor in open void. That looks like a mistake wearing the shape of a good idea. (2) rhizomatic_structure ships mutuality: "pockets", which its own source describes as '12 lateral chords' on '62 branches' — 'rhizomatic pockets in an otherwise tree-shaped growth'. The counter-image to hierarchy is currently mostly hierarchy; "total" is 100 chords with no traceable trunk and no branch more central than any other, and it is a one-token change on the placement. I agree with the thread that the blurb's Ford-Fulkerson paragraph and networkflow3d belong two rooms later in GT_Flow — tutorial.md here contains no flow at all, only degree, Brandes betweenness, eigenvector and closeness.

GT_Connectivity.for: Introduce direction, and be the one room whose architecture is the algorithm: three chambers you can fall out of and cannot climb back into. It is the room the second thread (measure / prune / cut / fold) skips, which is why it currently reads as a lecture wedged between two halves.
GT_Connectivity.claim: The three rooms the blurb promises were built; the wedges that would open them are placed one cell off. Structure has three chambers — left cols 1-4 at h1, middle cols 6-8 at h2, right cols 10-12 at h1 — split by wall columns at 5 and 9, with gaps at rows 4, 6, 7, 8 in col 5 and at row 4 only in col 9. The climbing wedge wp:270 sits at row 5 col 6, whose low side (5,5) is a h5 wall, so it climbs from nothing: today 43 of 140 cells are reachable, kosaraju_algorithm at (6,2) is unreachable, and so is the exit teleporter at (11,7).
GT_Connectivity.unsure: THIS READING CONTRADICTS the red-thread argument for this room. I disagree with the red-thread pass here. It reads the room as three artifacts on one row in a floor that does not exist — but the three chambers ARE in the structure layer, and the failure is two wedges off by a cell, not missing architecture. What I cannot settle: (1) whether Palle wants the one-wayness to come from wedge grammar at all. It would be honest — you can drop from h2 to h1 anywhere and only climb where a wedge stands, which is a real one-way door and would make the utility layer carry the whole lesson. (2) The right chamber holds no artifact, only the exit. Third component, or unfinished? The artifacts run 2 / 1 / 0 across the three rooms. (3) With the teleporter unreachable this map cannot be completed on foot, and map_pathfinder reports both facts as WARN, so it prints OK. Anyone writing final.md from the blurb would be describing a walk nobody can take.

GT_Spanning_Trees.for: Be the accountant's room — where the sequence stops describing networks and starts cutting them, and where the cut gets charged for. It only completes the argument the rhizome opened two halls back.
GT_Spanning_Trees.claim: This room cannot close on its own and its own walked.md says so: 'The rhizome two rooms back is what it looked like before.' One station cannot argue a trade; the pair can, and that pairing is the sequence's second, better thread. Meanwhile the floor makes the harder point by accident — six islands, 26 of 34 cells reachable, the h2 island at cols 7-8 and the h4 island at rows 6-7 stranded. The room is a spanning forest, which is what a spanning tree becomes when the graph will not connect.
GT_Spanning_Trees.unsure: I do not know whether the two stranded islands are an oversight or the argument. mst_visualization carries a backbone axis whose fourth value is literally "forest", and the placement runs the default "picked" — so the room could name what its own floor is doing with one token, but only if Palle wants the floor read as a graph at all. Second: the blurb says 'Narrow walkways connect them — each one an edge you walk, each platform a node you stand on', and there are exactly two walkway wedges in the map, at (4,5) and (5,5). Everything else called an edge is plain floor adjacency, and two of the nodes have no edge. Third, and this is the field I am least sure of: I chose relation over artifacts because with one station and a severed floor the room has nothing else to stand on, and because its own text names the room it depends on. If Palle wants it self-contained it needs a second artifact — the loopy graph before the cut, and a way to cut an edge and watch the tree fall in two, which is what intent.md's critical angle argues and nothing in the room performs.

GT_Flow.for: Be the room where the network breaks: where the sequence stops asking what can be reached and asks how much can pass, and where optimisation and destruction return the same number.
GT_Flow.claim: A room built as an elevation ships the elevation switched off. push_relabel_algorithm places at its default relief: "flat", which its own source defines as 'six 0.4 m spheres on a 4 m ring, all at y = 0, height and excess readable only as small text' — 'the algorithm's central quantity exists nowhere in space'. The value "terraced" builds the final push-relabel heights as a ~3 m stepped landscape with the sink at 0, the source on top and every edge visibly running downhill. One token, on one placement, in the one room whose floor is already a funnel.
GT_Flow.unsure: I agree with the thread that the registers disagree on mechanism and I cannot settle which side Palle keeps. blurb and the placed artifact are push-relabel ('local panic. No global view'); tutorial.md opens 'Max flow from source to sink. Edmonds-Karp via BFS' and contains no push and no relabel anywhere in 118 lines. Cutting the blurb loses the room's best paragraph; cutting the tutorial loses its only working code. Second, unverified: the funnel is real — 11 open cells at row 1 narrowing to 3 by row 8, spawn at the wide end, exit at the throat — but col 11 is a separate 1-wide corridor running rows 1 to 10 that dead-ends at the bottom. A pipe that reaches no sink carries zero flow, which is either the sharpest thing in the room or an unnoticed leftover. Third: grid3d_dfs at (2,1) and grid3d_prim at (10,1) flank the wide entrance — a search piece and a spanning-tree piece guarding a flow room, both belonging to earlier halls. karger_algorithm ships bottleneck: "mixed"; "severed" is the cut this room's theorem is about.

GT_Matching.for: Close the sequence, and with it all 22 spine sequences, on the one problem where the obstruction is folded rather than deleted. As shipped it also closes on the gap between what an algorithm promises and what it does.
GT_Matching.claim: The room is placed at the value that hides its subject. edmonds_algorithm:0:0:0.6 carries no config token, so coupling runs its default "partial" — a greedy pass that leaves a few vertices over; the file's own header reads 'Edmonds' Algorithm: Maximum Matching (Simplified Greedy Version)' and its @identity says 'greedy maximum matching', which is exactly what the blurb dismisses. The value "blossom", which 'builds the odd cycle greed cannot solve', exists and is unused, while the floor is four-fold symmetric — mirrored left-right and top-bottom, the even, bipartite-shaped case intent.md calls easy.
GT_Matching.unsure: I cannot settle whether this is a defect or the room's real subject, and only Palle can pick. Written one way the text says the honest thing — here is greed failing, the fix is not in this room, and every formal system has an outside, which is a strong ending for this curriculum. Written the other way the placement gets #coupling:blossom (a word value, so safe from the number-becomes-rotation trap), the odd pentagon appears, and the room finally shows what the blurb has been promising. These are two different rooms. Second: tutorial.md is mostly the easy case — bipartite, greedy, Hopcroft-Karp, a hungarian() whose body is '# Full Hungarian loop omitted for brevity', an 8-line contract_blossom stub, Gale-Shapley — so nothing in the room performs the contraction at any layer. Third: walked.md ends with 'The seed (missing)' — the chamber that would carry graph theory forward was dropped from the spine on 2026-09-02, so this room currently closes the whole spine on an acknowledged hole, and I do not know whether final.md should carry that hole or ignore it.

QFEP_Introduction.for: The only room where all four terms are turnable at once. qfep_balance_workbench at (2,2) has F, E, lambda and phi on one tilted plate and recomputes QFE live; the six rooms after it take the four apart one at a time. This is the whole shape, held once, before it is dismantled.
QFEP_Introduction.claim: The room hands you the formula as a balance you crank, and withholds one hand: F, E and lambda are grabbable spheres at (4,2), (2,9), (3,9), phi is only a slider — so the term the sequence calls queer is the one term you cannot hold until the last room of the sequence.
QFEP_Introduction.unsure: Whether the missing grab_sphere_phi is a decision or an oversight. grab_sphere_phi is placed in QFEP_Synthesis and nowhere else on the spine; intent.md's own Key artifacts line also lists only F, E and lambda, so the omission is at least consistent — but the blurb promises 'Touch each term: F, E, lambda, phi'. If it is an oversight the claim inverts into a placement fix and this brief is wrong. Second: the tt at (2,1) keys `qfep_introduction`, which exists only as an orphan .md — it is not in tutorial_text.json (only entropy_axioms is, in the whole sequence), so the room's opening words render blank, and standing 3 cells away is synthesis_stand#subject:tt#mode:hero, which exhibits how tutorial text is MOUNTED. A blank mount beside an exhibit of mounts is either the sharpest joke in the sequence or a coincidence; I cannot tell which and it changes the text. Third: I agree with the argument's 'recognized, not learned', but the workbench's retrospection is to the PROJECT's seven timeline phases (hard-coded PHASE_COLORS), not to the player's own walk — and no text in the room names the workbench at all.

QFEP_F_Term.for: The one room that lets order win. lambda_slider is placed with #locked:0, the puzzles snap shut, the crystal is beautiful — it exists so success can be felt in the hands before the sequence names the cost.
QFEP_F_Term.claim: F's terminus is not waiting at the end of the corridor, it is the cell you spawn in: dark_sphere sits at (1,1) on the spawn point, so you begin inside the dark room and the puzzles walk you out of it.
QFEP_F_Term.unsure: This contradicts the room's own texts, not the argument. blurb.md says 'the dark room awaits'; critical.md line 9 puts 'the dark sphere at the corridor's end'. Both describe a walk toward it; the grid puts it under your feet at frame one. Palle rules: move the sphere south to (1,9) beside crystal_cluster and the existing texts become true, or keep it at spawn and the final.md argues the inversion (order's endpoint is where you already are). I lean to keeping it, but I would not write either without the ruling. Second thing worth his eye: nothing in this room was built for it. dark_sphere stands in 342 maps and is registered in lsystems.json as an 'atmospheric and geometric reference'; science_screen 252; crystal_cluster 32; shannon_workbench 24. The only local decision is the config token `#locked:0`. That is a real observation about the room but it is closer to a repair note than to prose, and I could not settle whether it belongs in the text.

QFEP_E_Term.for: The only room that makes entropy a number you can count rather than a texture you look at. microstate_counter, entropy_fan and possibility_space_cloud are purpose-built and near-unique (placed in 3, 2 and 5 maps in the whole corpus); everywhere else in the curriculum entropy is shown as mess.
QFEP_E_Term.claim: E is a count, and a count needs a box: microstate_counter's W is cells^N with the cells chosen by hand, and unsealing the jar makes the ledger print nothing — so the room's freedom is bounded by an act of enclosure it performs off-stage.
QFEP_E_Term.unsure: The whole room stands in rows 2 and 3. All six bodies are there; the raised plateau at rows 4-8 is empty; the two labels POSSIBILITY SPACE (2,7) and lambda=1 DISSOLUTION (2,11) hang over nine rows of nothing between the instruments and the teleporter at (6,12). Either the emptiness IS dissolution argued in floor plan — which would be the best thing in the room and would make me want core=utilities — or it is an unfinished placement and the labels are captions with no subject. The answer decides whether the final.md describes a bench or a walk. Also: tutorial.md's freeze button claims 'entropy is a rate, not a property', which none of the three instruments supports (they all measure a count over a fixed configuration space); I would cut that line rather than carry it.

QFEP_Lambda_Spectrum.for: The hinge. The only room where F and E stand in one space and where the sequence stops describing lambda and makes you be it — eighteen rows of corridor with six signs down its left edge.
QFEP_Lambda_Spectrum.claim: The corridor's caption spine is the entire argument and the bodies contradict it: nothing stands at lambda=0.0 ORDER (2,4), and ordered_grid (4,19), crystal_formation (2,20) and complexity_pattern (1,20) are all SOUTH of the lambda=1.0 CHAOS sign at (2,17) — while the room's best object, lambda_hall, is in the eastern half behind the height-2 ridge at x=5 that the walk from spawn (1,1) to the exit (3,18) never crosses.
QFEP_Lambda_Spectrum.unsure: THIS READING CONTRADICTS the red-thread argument for this room. I disagree with the red-thread essay's remedy. It says fix the corridor's order and the first six rooms are a straight line into the edge. But lambda_hall is a 14 m walk-in whose west wall is a frozen lattice, whose east wall is the same lattice boiling, and whose only lit floor is a narrow walkway at lambda 0.35 — it is the room, already built, placed in exactly one map in the corpus, and it is standing in the half nobody enters. Reordering six signs leaves the better version of the room in the corner. My reading is that the cheap fix is to put the walk through lambda_hall and demote the labelled strip to a caption — which flips core to artifacts and rewrites the brief. I also disagree with critical.md, which argues at length that the vestibular system reads a continuous descent as 'heights descend from 1 to 0': the structure layer is height 1 flat for rows 1-17 and only drops at rows 18-20, after the last sign. The gradient that text is built on is not in the grid. Third, unresolved: qfep_chalkboard at (2,3) states the whole formula at the corridor's mouth — it is the only placement of that artifact anywhere — and I could not decide whether it belongs here or in the Introduction.

QFEP_Phi_Term.for: The only room that asks you to pick a side. The floor is split at x=5 with phi_slider on the seam, RESIST west, EMBRACE east, and you cannot stand in both halves.
QFEP_Phi_Term.claim: Phi is argued by which bodies own a clock: rigid_sculpture and preserved_pattern have no `_process` at all, so resistance is not a setting the room turns down but time deleted from the file — and the phi_slider at (5,5) connects to none of the four.
QFEP_Phi_Term.unsure: The blurb's 'Move the phi slider and feel the difference' is the one thing the room cannot do. Nothing in rigid_sculpture.gd, preserved_pattern.gd, fluid_form.gd or transforming_pattern.gd joins or reads a slider group; the only script that joins 'qfep_phi_controllers' is qfep_sandbox_console, which is placed in Gallery_QFEP, not here. Write the text after the wire, or write it about the absence — but the absence is arguably the better argument, because a slider that changes nothing IS what negative phi looks like from the inside, and I could not settle whether that is a reading or an excuse. Separately: lambda_promenade sits at (3,7), on the RESIST side. It is an eight-station synthesis rail about the LAMBDA axis, standing in a room about phi, on the conservative half. Deliberate (the resisting side is the one that displays the whole spectrum as a museum row) or a misplacement? It is the only thing in the sequence I could not read at all.

QFEP_Edge_Of_Chaos.for: The room where the sequence stops arguing and lets you stand somewhere. It is the only room that puts two kinds of knowing three cells apart and refuses to rank them.
QFEP_Edge_Of_Chaos.claim: Being held at the edge and being handed the dial are different knowings, and the room makes that claim by geometry rather than text: lambda_slider#locked:0.4 at (10,2) and edge_of_chaos_unlocked at (13,4), close enough that you meet the withholding and its refusal in one glance.
QFEP_Edge_Of_Chaos.unsure: The floor is the only floor in the sequence shaped like its own argument — a four-step mound rising 1-2-3-4 to a summit plateau at rows 6-9 — and nothing stands on it. All six artifacts are on the flat rim at row 2 and at (13,4); the summit holds one overhead light. Is the empty summit the point (the edge is a location, not an object — tutorial.md's own line) or an unfinished placement? That ruling changes the shape of the text more than anything else here. Second: edge_core at (7,2) is on the rim, and its own header states that nothing in the repository calls its set_lambda(), so the core of the edge room is frozen at its initialiser and shows one state forever. Third: the tt at (2,1) keys `edge_of_chaos`, an orphan .md not in tutorial_text.json, so the room's words render blank.

QFEP_Sandbox.for: The room where the promise comes due. lambda_slider is placed in four rooms of this sequence and pinned in three of them — #locked:0 in F_Term, #value:1.0 in E_Term, #locked:0.4 in Edge_Of_Chaos — and this is the fourth, unpinned. The room has no labels at all, because its whole content is the release of three earlier locks.
QFEP_Sandbox.claim: The release is real and the handoff is not: qfep_reactor.gd:431 and reactive_particle_field.gd:297 wait on the group "qfep_slider", nothing in the repository ever joins it, and lambda_slider joins "qfep_lambda_controllers" instead — so the one room in the sequence where the dial is free is the one room where turning it moves nothing.
QFEP_Sandbox.unsure: Two things Palle has to rule. (1) The core call. I have said `relation` because both blurb.md and intent.md define this room by negation of the six before it ('No more guided tours. No locked sliders.'), and because the four settings of one artifact token are the sequence's real spine. But it does have its own furniture — the reactor on a height-3 podium at (7,4), sliders on the flat at (5,1) and (9,1) — so `artifacts` is a defensible fallback and would produce a very different text. (2) Whether to wire it first. The working pair exists: qfep_sandbox_console joins both controller groups and edge_of_chaos_orb reads both — and they are placed in Gallery_QFEP and Ribbon_Qfeplaboratory_04, never on the spine. Run that wire and the final.md is about your own lambda; leave it and the final.md is a control desk with the cable cut, which is colder, sharper, and arguably the honest end of a sequence about instruments that cannot reach their own limit. I lean to running the wire, but the second text is the better one and I do not want to talk myself out of saying so.

QFEP_Synthesis.for: The closing room, and the only one that turns the instruments on themselves. entropy_ceiling — the sequence's own registered seam, placed in exactly one map in the corpus — stands at (3,6) showing a quantized meter pinned at MAX with the true value in amber above the last tick.
QFEP_Synthesis.claim: What you carry out is not mastery but an instrument that knows its ceiling: the four terms return as bodies at (5,2), (2,10), (3,10), (4,10), grasp_cabinet at (3,8) shows all four spheres are literally ONE SCENE under five theories of a handle, and entropy_ceiling shows the meter cannot reach the value it reports.
QFEP_Synthesis.unsure: Three things, and the first is load-bearing. (1) THE PLINTH OF BECOMING at (6,5) labels the raised height-3 plateau at rows 5-8, lit by el:3:1 at (6,6), and NOTHING stands on it.
